Posted by Jim Brewer on May 10th, 2018 // No Comments
Security National Trust Co. lowered its holdings in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 2.3% during the 4th quarter, Holdings Channel reports. The firm owned 55,804 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 1,310 shares during the period. Apple makes up about 3.0% of Security National Trust Co.’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 5th largest holding. Security National Trust Co.’s holdings in Apple were worth $9,443,000 at the end of the most recent quarter.
A number of other hedge funds have also bought and sold shares of the business. Fulcrum Capital LLC purchased a new position in Apple in the fourth quarter worth $9,064,000. Torch Wealth Management LLC boosted its position in Apple by 2.2% in the fourth quarter. Torch Wealth Management LLC now owns 47,929 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $8,111,000 after purchasing an additional 1,038 shares during the last quarter. AMI Investment Management Inc. purchased a new position in Apple in the fourth quarter worth $225,000. Meridian Wealth Management LLC boosted its position in Apple by 4.6% in the fourth quarter. Meridian Wealth Management LLC now owns 17,721 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,846,000 after purchasing an additional 783 shares during the last quarter. Finally, Lyell Wealth Management LP boosted its position in Apple by 2.9% in the fourth quarter. Lyell Wealth Management LP now owns 31,361 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,307,000 after purchasing an additional 874 shares during the last quarter. 61.12% of the stock is currently owned by institutional investors and hedge funds. AAPL opened at $187.36 on Thursday. The company has a current ratio of 1.46, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80. The stock has a market capitalization of $944.02 billion, a P/E ratio of 17.96, a P/E/G ratio of 1.38 and a beta of 1.26. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The business had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same period last year, the company earned $2.10 EPS. Apple’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. analysts predict that Apple will post 11.43 earnings per share for the current year.
Apple declared that its board has initiated a stock repurchase program on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock buyback programs are generally an indication that the company’s board of directors believes its shares are undervalued.
The business also recently declared a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Investors of record on Monday, May 14th will be given a dividend of $0.73 per share. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.56%. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date is Friday, May 11th. Apple’s dividend payout ratio (DPR) is presently 27.36%.
In related news, insider Angela J. Ahrendts sold 38,228 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, May 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $176.54, for a total transaction of $6,748,771.12. Following the transaction, the insider now directly owns 90,967 shares in the company, valued at approximately $16,059,314.18. The transaction was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which is available through this hyperlink . Also, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total value of $11,564,692.22. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last 90 days, insiders have sold 164,216 shares of company stock worth $28,084,972. 0.06% of the stock is owned by corporate insiders.
AAPL has been the topic of several research analyst reports. Bank of America cut Apple from a “buy” rating to a “neutral” rating and boosted their price objective for the stock from $180.00 to $220.00 in a research report on Wednesday, January 17th. Cascend Securities boosted their price objective on Apple from $200.00 to $220.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Monday, January 29th. Morgan Stanley reaffirmed a “buy” rating and set a $205.00 price target (up previously from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research report on Tuesday, January 23rd. Rosenblatt Securities reaffirmed a “buy” rating and set a $180.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research report on Friday, January 19th. Finally, Maxim Group upped their price target on Apple from $193.00 to $204.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research report on Friday, January 12th. One equities research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have given a hold rating, thirty-three have issued a buy rating and two have assigned a strong buy rating to the company. Apple has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $204.00.
About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
